explanation: Initial TR is 2000; new TR is 12×180 = 2160. The quantity response is proportionately smaller than the price rise, so revenue increases.

prompt: A firm faces a straight-line downward-sloping demand curve and sells at its midpoint. What happens to total revenue after a small but non-zero price cut along this curve?

options.label: A
options.text: TR rises because quantity sold increases.

options.label: B
options.text: TR stays unchanged despite a lower price.

options.label: C
options.text: TR falls from its initial maximum.

options.label: D
options.text: TR becomes zero because MR equals zero.

explanation: If P = a − bQ, total revenue is aQ − bQ² and is maximised at the demand midpoint Q = a/(2b). Any non-zero movement away reduces revenue. Unit elasticity describes the instantaneous percentage offset at the midpoint, not unchanged revenue after a finite price change.

prompt: A firm is on the elastic upper section of a straight-line demand curve. As it lowers price toward the midpoint, what happens?

options.label: A
options.text: TR falls; MR is negative.

options.label: B
options.text: TR stays unchanged; MR is zero throughout.

options.label: C
options.text: MR and AR stay equal throughout.

options.label: D
options.text: TR rises; MR reaches zero at the midpoint.

explanation: On the elastic region, price cuts increase TR. MR is positive until it reaches zero at unit elasticity.

options.label: C

prompt: If the same oligopolist cuts price slightly below P*, why might the quantity sold increase only slightly?

options.label: A
options.text: Rivals leave prices unchanged, producing large sales gains.

options.label: B
options.text: Demand below the kink becomes more price elastic.

options.label: C
options.text: Rivals match the cut, limiting extra sales.

options.label: D
options.text: The original oligopoly becomes a single-supplier monopoly.

explanation: Below the kink, matched price cuts make demand relatively inelastic, limiting the sales gain from a lower price.

prompt: The firm’s MC curve shifts upward but remains within the vertical discontinuity of MR. What happens in the kinked-demand model?

options.label: C
options.text: The firm’s demand necessarily becomes horizontal.

options.label: D
